long_biography.plain_text:
Trading Russian sable in London placed Farkhad Akhmedov at the meeting point of Soviet commodities and Western markets. In 1987 he founded Tansley Trading to supply equipment to Russian gas producers, then began acquiring shares in Nortgas. He took control of the Siberian producer after buying another investor's holding and became its chairman.

Akhmedov sold his remaining Nortgas interest in 2012, converting an operating energy stake into investment capital. In Baku, his collecting took institutional form through Nar Gallery, conceived as a permanent public display. Its name came from his first acquisition, Togrul Narimanbekov's Pomegranates, and its holdings join recognised and nonconformist artists within an account of twentieth-century Azerbaijani painting.
